When the AI Gateway streams a response c.body:
Each provider file defines a stateless ProviderAdapter subclass (classmethods converting OpenAI-style gateway payloads to/from the vendor wire format) and a BaseProvider subclass (config, headers, URLs, HTTP calls).

Gemini: mlflow/gateway/providers/gemini.py:GeminiAdapter (chat_to_model, model_to_chat, model_to_chat_streaming, completions_to_model, model_to_completions(_streaming), embeddings_to_model, model_to_embeddings) and GeminiProvider (_chat, _chat_stream, _completions, _completions_stream, _embeddings, _passthrough, _proxy). Flow in _chat: jsonable_encoder(payload, exclude_none=True) -> check_for_model_field -> adapter.chat_to_model -> send_request to {base_url}/{model}:generateContent -> adapter.model_to_chat. Streaming uses send_stream_request with :streamGenerateContent?alt=sse, handle_incomplete_chunks, strip_sse_prefix, then model_to_chat_streaming per chunk. Gemini completions are routed through chat_to_model.

Anthropic: providers/anthropic.py:AnthropicAdapter and AnthropicProvider (inherits both BaseProvider and AnthropicAdapter). _chat_stream tracks message_start metadata and accumulated usage in _usage_data, passed to AnthropicAdapter.model_to_chat_streaming. Embeddings are NotImplementedError.

LiteLLM: providers/litellm.py:LiteLLMProvider is a fallback; the adapter mostly validates OpenAI-shaped dicts. All kwargs go through _prepare_litellm_kwargs (destination/SSRF guard) before litellm calls. _passthrough dispatches on PassthroughAction.

TypeSafe: providers/typesafe.py:TypeSafeProvider supports only passthrough (TYPESAFE_SYSTEM_ONE, no streaming) and usage extraction.

Passthrough: PASSTHROUGH_PROVIDER_PATHS maps PassthroughAction to a vendor path; _validate_passthrough_action checks it; _extract_passthrough_token_usage and _extract_streaming_token_usage feed tracing usage.

When the tracking server is under heavy.title: Fail-closed net and gating invariants
answers: Why does my new route return 403 under fail-closed mode?
Which after-request handlers may be listed as self-authorizing?
Do admins skip after-request handlers?
When the tracking server is under heavy.body:
Every route must resolve an authorization decision. Under MLFLOW_BASIC_AUTH_FAIL_CLOSED, _before_request denies a request that has no validator unless _authorized_outside_before_request is true: path matches _PUBLIC_ROUTE_SUFFIXES or _HANDLER_INTERNAL_AUTHZ_SUFFIXES (matched with _matches_route_suffix after _strip_static_prefix, anchored to /api/N.N or /ajax-api/N.N), or its after-request handler is in _SELF_AUTHORIZING_AFTER_REQUEST_HANDLERS.

Only response filters/redactors count as self-authorizing. Ownership-grant and cleanup after-handlers run after a write that was already authorized, so never add them to _SELF_AUTHORIZING_AFTER_REQUEST_HANDLERS.

_KNOWN_UNGATED_ROUTE_MARKERS and _KNOWN_UNGATED_FASTAPI_ROUTE_MARKERS are intentionally empty; additions should be temporary tracked exceptions. Marker matching is segment-anchored (_is_known_ungated_route).

Prefix families in _find_validator (datasets, jobs, issues, traces) fail closed on unknown subpaths. Keep that.

Admins skip validators in both Flask (_before_request) and FastAPI (fastapi_permission_middleware), but after-request handlers still run for them (grant cleanup must not be bypassed). Response filters begin with `if sender_is_admin(): return`.

After-handlers are skipped on 4xx/5xx and are not authorization points, so failures are logged rather than raised where the main operation already succeeded (see _seed_default_workspace_roles, _cleanup_workspace_permissions).

Registered models and prompts share REST endpoints: classify by _entity_is_prompt / _request_targets_prompt and sweep or grant in both the 'registered_model' and 'prompt' namespaces (rename_registered_model_permission, delete_can_manage_registered_model_permission).

On a registered model that uses stages,.title: Model registry stores: SQL vs file backends overview
answers: Which store implementations exist and how do they differ?
How is the SQL store's session/engine set up, including read replicas?
How does the file store lay out data on disk?
On a registered model that uses stages,.body:
Two concrete implementations of mlflow.store.model_registry.abstract_store:AbstractStore live here.

SqlAlchemyStore (sqlalchemy_store.py:SqlAlchemyStore) is the main backend. __init__ gets a cached engine from _get_or_create_engine (class-level _engine_map guarded by _engine_map_lock), creates tables if missing, calls _verify_registry_tables_exist, and builds self.ManagedSessionMaker. If read_db_uri differs from db_uri it uses _get_routing_session_maker (reads go to the replica, writes use `read_only=False`). Otherwise it uses _get_managed_session_maker. Finally it runs _initialize_store_state, which raises INVALID_STATE if any registered model or webhook exists outside DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_NAME.

FileStore (file_store.py:FileStore) is the maintenance-mode filesystem backend. The constructor raises unless MLFLOW_ALLOW_FILE_STORE is set. Layout: <root>/models/<name>/meta.yaml, plus tags/ and aliases/ folders and version-N/ dirs, each with their own meta.yaml and tags/. Search is done in Python: it loads everything and uses SearchModelUtils.filter/sort and SearchModelVersionUtils. file_store._validate_model_name adds path-separator and '%' checks on top of the shared validator. FileModelVersion carries storage_location.

Both stores implement the same public methods: registered model CRUD, create_model_version, stage transition, tags, aliases, search_*. Webhook methods exist only in SqlAlchemyStore. Behavior changes to the shared API usually have to be made in both files.

Common flow in SQL: validate inputs, open ManagedSessionMaker, load the ORM row via _get_registered_model or _get_sql_model_version, mutate it, then return to_mlflow_entity(), usually via _populate_model_version_aliases.

Copying or serializing trace data fails.title: Span class hierarchy and creation
answers: Which span class do I get from an OTel span?
How does LazySpan defer parsing?
Why does span['x'] or span.get raise?
Copying or serializing trace data fails.body:
mlflow/entities/span.py wraps OpenTelemetry spans. Always build spans via create_mlflow_span: NonRecordingSpan or falsy gives NoOpSpan; an OTel Span (recording) gives LiveSpan; an OTel ReadableSpan gives immutable Span; anything else raises MlflowException.

Classes:
- Span: immutable, finished span. Holds _span (OTel), _attributes (_CachedSpanAttributesRegistry), _attachments, _links. Getters (inputs, outputs, span_type, log_level, description, model_name, llm_cost) all go through get_attribute and SpanAttributeKey. trace_id comes from the REQUEST_ID attribute, not from the OTel context; _trace_id is the OTel hex id.
- LiveSpan(Span): mutable, does NOT call super().__init__. Uses _SpanAttributesRegistry, and sets REQUEST_ID and SPAN_TYPE attributes on construction. Setters: set_inputs, set_outputs, set_attribute(s), set_status, add_event, add_link, record_exception, end. LiveSpan.to_immutable_span downcasts to Span; LiveSpan.from_immutable_span clones a span into the current trace via the InMemoryTraceManager.
- LazySpan(Span): holds the stored dict and materializes through Span.from_dict on first attribute access (__getattr__ then _ensure_materialized). It writes through __dict__ deliberately. to_dict returns the live dict and clears _raw_json. json_for_export uses the raw JSON if untouched.
- NoOpSpan: all setters are no-ops and getters return None. trace_id is NO_OP_SPAN_TRACE_ID.

Span deliberately blocks dict-style use: __getitem__ raises a TypeError with hints, __iter__ is None, and __getattr__ gives a special message for 'get'. Don't add a get method or subscripting.

answers: How do I add a new passthrough endpoint?
Where do I wire a new provider's credentials into the gateway?
What do I need for a streaming passthrough?
Endpoints in the AI Gateway that use the.body:
New passthrough route:
1. Add a PassthroughAction and its PASSTHROUGH_ROUTES entry in mlflow/gateway/providers/base.py, and implement the action in the provider's passthrough.
2. Add a GatewayInvocationType (mlflow/telemetry/events) and GatewayRequestType (mlflow/gateway/config) value.
3. In mlflow/server/gateway_api.py add a handler decorated like the others: @gateway_router.post(PASSTHROUGH_ROUTES[...], response_model=None), @translate_http_exception, @_record_gateway_invocation(...).
4. Copy the standard pipeline from an existing handler such as anthropic_passthrough_messages: body, model extraction, _validate_store, _create_provider_from_endpoint_name, _set_gateway_telemetry_state, check_budget_limit, _get_guardrails_and_auth, guarded closure, maybe_traced_gateway_call with make_budget_on_complete. For streaming, add an aggregate_*_stream_chunks reducer in mlflow/gateway/tracing_utils and pass it as output_reducer. Pass message_format if the payload is not OpenAI-shaped.
5. If the route is not Flask/auth-routed already, check the auth permission mapping for the path.

New provider: add the Provider enum and Config class in mlflow/gateway/config, register it in get_provider, then add a branch in _build_endpoint_config in gateway_api.py that builds the config from model_config.auth_config (non-secret, e.g. api_base) and model_config.secret_value (secrets). Providers with no branch fall through to LiteLLM; the branch may rewrite model_config.provider (Azure becomes OPENAI, Databricks, Bedrock). Gate on is_provider_allowed first. Keep the ordering of the existing branches.

Searching MCP access endpoints by the na.title: SearchUtils class hierarchy and how to add a searchable entity
answers: How is a filter string parsed and evaluated?
What must a new SearchUtils subclass define?
Where are SQL dialect comparison differences handled?
Searching MCP access endpoints by the na.body:
mlflow/utils/search_utils.py parses filter and order_by strings with sqlparse and evaluates them in memory. `SearchUtils` is the run-oriented base class. Each entity gets a subclass that overrides class attributes and a few hooks.

Pipeline: `SearchUtils.parse_search_filter` calls sqlparse and then `_process_statement`. That calls `_join_in_comparison_tokens`, which merges IN, NOT IN, IS NULL and IS NOT NULL into Comparison tokens. `_invalid_statement_token_*` rejects anything that is not a Comparison or AND. `_get_comparison` runs `_validate_comparison`, `_get_identifier` and `_get_value`, and produces dicts `{type, key, comparator, value}`. Matching goes through `_does_*_match_clause`, which uses `is_*` checks (they validate comparators against `VALID_*_COMPARATORS`) and `get_comparison_func`. SQL stores use `get_sql_comparison_func(comparator, dialect)`, which has per-dialect variants for POSTGRES, SQLITE, MSSQL and MYSQL. MySQL and MSSQL force case-sensitive comparison on string columns.

To add a new entity (as SearchIssuesUtils, SearchMCPServerUtils and SearchEvaluationDatasetsUtils do):
1. Subclass SearchUtils and set VALID_SEARCH_ATTRIBUTE_KEYS, NUMERIC_ATTRIBUTES and, if sorting is needed, VALID_ORDER_BY_ATTRIBUTE_KEYS.
2. Set LIST_SUPPORTED_KEYS, the frozenset of keys allowed with IN lists. An empty frozenset disables lists. `SearchUtils.validate_list_supported` enforces it.
3. Override `_process_statement` and `_get_comparison` only if the identifier grammar differs. Base `_get_identifier` assumes run-style prefixes (metric, param, tag, attribute, dataset). Others define their own: registered models and versions use attribute, tag and tags only.
4. Override comparator sets such as VALID_TAG_COMPARATORS where they differ.
5. For in-memory sort, build a `_get_sort_key` that wraps values with `_apply_reversor` and `_Reversor` for descending order. Always append tie-breakers (for example name, or timestamp and request_id).

SearchTraceUtils is the exception: it calls `_join_in_comparison_tokens(..., search_traces=True)`, and it maps search keys through SEARCH_KEY_TO_TAG, SEARCH_KEY_TO_METADATA and SEARCH_KEY_TO_SPAN in `_replace_key_to_tag_or_metadata`. Span and assessment filters are DB-only. Pagination tokens for runs use `SearchUtils.paginate`.

When I send a chat request to a Gemini o.title: How to change chat request translation (new OpenAI param, tool, or content type)
answers: How do I add a new OpenAI parameter mapping for Gemini?
Where are tools and response_format converted?
Why is my Gemini parameter missing from generationConfig?
When I send a chat request to a Gemini o.body:
Edit the adapter's chat_to_model, and the matching response method if output changes.

Gemini (gemini.py:GeminiAdapter.chat_to_model): scalar params need an entry in GENERATION_CONFIG_KEY_MAPPING (OpenAI name -> Gemini camelCase) AND the camelCase name in GENERATION_CONFIGS, otherwise they are dropped from generationConfig. The camelCase names are rejected with 422 if sent directly (the loop over the mapping). max_completion_tokens is folded into max_tokens. Messages: user/assistant -> contents with role user/model; system messages collect into system_instruction; tool messages become functionResponse parts, merged into the previous user turn if it is all functionResponse (parallel calls). response_format maps to generationConfig responseJsonSchema/responseMimeType; tools become functionDeclarations with parametersJsonSchema. Multimodal content goes through _to_gemini_parts; tool results through _tool_result_to_response.

Anthropic (anthropic.py:AnthropicAdapter.chat_to_model): stop->stop_sequences, max_tokens defaulted and capped by the MLFLOW_AI_GATEWAY_ANTHROPIC_* constants, n must be 1, temperature is halved, system messages joined with newline, tool_calls become tool_use blocks, tool messages become user tool_result, tool_choice via match, response_format json_schema goes through _enforce_strict_schema (falls back to plain text on _UnsupportedSchemaError), json_object adds a system instruction.
